27:## Further prior work for Related Work (added for paper-repo#7 M4)
## Further prior work for Related Work (added for paper-repo#7 M4)
Each item: the sentence of related work it supports, and how it differs from our claim. Metadata of every entry was checked against arXiv, the ACL Anthology or Crossref. Entries for Rodriguez et al. 2021 and Miller 2024 are kept in `paper-repo`'s bibliography and not repeated here.

**Item response theory for model evaluation** (sentence: "IRT, from psychometrics, was brought to NLP and ML evaluation to separate item difficulty from model ability").
- lalor-etal-2016-building (IRT scale for NLP test sets), martinezplumed2019irt (IRT for ML classifiers at the instance level), vania-etal-2021-comparing (IRT to compare test sets and their discriminating power). They use IRT to *describe* items and test sets. Ours uses an item-level difficulty only as a *covariate* whose error is corrected by a probability sample; no claim about the latent model is needed.
- chen2025compact (compact IRT representations of LLM abilities for routing and performance prediction on new benchmarks) and shnitzer2023routing (benchmark results used to choose an LLM for a new task): model-based prediction across tasks, not an estimate of the same benchmark's mean from a sample of its items.

**Adaptive and amortized evaluation** (sentence: "adaptive testing picks the next item by the current ability estimate; amortized IRT reduces the cost of calibrating items").
- zhuang2023adaptive (the arXiv version is a position paper arguing for psychometric adaptive testing of AI models instead of a fixed test set; our IRT-CAT baseline is this family); truong2025amortized (predicts question difficulty from question content so IRT needs no per-item calibration on many models, and uses a difficulty-conditioned question generator for adaptive testing; as an estimator it is model-based). Both choose items by information, so the inclusion probabilities are unknown and the estimate is model-based and biased when the model is wrong. Ours keeps known inclusion probabilities. They are the right comparators for the CAT cell of the design grid (hofmann2025fluid, balkir2026confident likewise).
- prabhu2024lifelong (Sort & Search: reuses previously evaluated models to rank test samples and sub-select a subset for accuracy estimation, on image classification benchmarks, Lifelong-CIFAR10 and Lifelong-ImageNet). Closest to ours in taking earlier models' item results as the covariate for item selection and in estimating accuracy from a subset. Differs: it is evaluated on image classifiers, not LLM benchmarks, and its estimate carries no design-based bias correction; it does not study targets stronger than all sources.

**Estimating a benchmark's score and its noise** (sentence: "a benchmark score is a sample mean over a finite item set; its sampling variance is non-negligible").
- madaan2024variance (variance sources in benchmark scores, including the item-sampling component); owen2024predictable (benchmark scores as a function of compute: the extrapolation target in the other direction, from model scale instead of from other models' items); ruan2024observational (a low-dimensional capability space built from many models predicts held-out, larger models' benchmark scores; closest in spirit to our source-matrix predictor, but it predicts from aggregate benchmark scores and compute of other models, not from a few items of the same benchmark).
- yax2024phylolm (output similarity as a predictor of benchmark performance across LLM families; motivates our lineage-held-out split). Differs: no per-item sample of the target's own answers.

**Statistically principled evaluation with a proxy** (sentence: "prediction-powered estimators combine a cheap predictor with a labelled sample and keep validity").

\section{Related work}
\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Predicting a benchmark score from few items.}
Anchor points~\citep{vivek2024anchor} keep the medoids of clusters of items with similar source responses and average the target's answers on them with cluster-size weights; tinyBenchmarks~\citep{maiapolo2024tiny} fit an item-response-theory (IRT) ability of the target on such anchors; metabench~\citep{kipnis2025metabench} selects items by IRT information and regresses with a generalized additive model.
Others learn a predictor of the target's success on unseen items from a few reference items~\citep{pacchiardi2024100}, an adaptive acquisition policy with a neural predictor~\citep{li2025active}, items that target the model's ability~\citep{hofmann2025fluid,balkir2026confident}, or a predictor of rank correlation to choose subsets~\citep{saranathan-etal-2025-sublime}.
Most are \emph{model-based predictors} with empirical support on held-out models that resemble the sources.
We use the score matrices released with a comparison of such methods~\citep{zhang2025miss} as data; we use neither its code nor its findings.
Item response theory has been used to reweight and diagnose leaderboards~\citep{rodriguez2021evaluation}, and statistical treatments of evaluation data stress uncertainty over items~\citep{miller2024errorbars}.
Related are the aggregation of sparse sample-level measurements~\citep{ghosh2024onebench} and cost reduction by dropping items or configurations~\citep{perlitz-etal-2024-efficient}.

\paragraph{Estimation with a free covariate.}
Estimating the mean of a finite population from a sample, with an auxiliary variable known for every unit, is the subject of model-assisted survey estimation: generalized-regression and difference estimators use auxiliary predictions to reduce variance and remain design-unbiased~\citep{sarndal1992model}.
Prediction-powered inference~\citep{angelopoulos2023ppi,angelopoulos2023ppiplus} transplants the idea to machine-learning predictions, with a power-tuned weight on the predictions, and active statistical inference~\citep{zrnic2024active} draws the labelled points with probabilities that follow the model's uncertainty.
The latter is the closest to our design and estimator.
It differs in the covariate (here a matrix of source-model results on every item, not one model's uncertainty), in the finite binary population with fixed-size designs and a positivity floor, and in the target, which includes the \emph{ordering} of models.
Active testing~\citep{kossen2021active,yilmaz2021sample} selects items by importance sampling with a surrogate trained for one model; prediction-powered ranking~\citep{chatzi2024prediction} ranks LLMs from human preferences; and subgroup accuracy~\citep{fogliato-etal-2024-precise} combines direct and regression estimates.

shown.message:
`dev` has two more pushes: the related-work references from idea-repo, and two checks added to Section 5. The built document is clean (29 pages, no undefined references). `paper-repo`#7 is still waiting on two other roles.

- **References:** I merged idea-repo's 13 new entries into `references.bib` (58 entries, up from 45). Related work now has sentences citing them, including the two nearest to our setting: Prabhu et al. (2024) on lifelong evaluation, and Ruan et al. (2024) on predicting larger models' scores. I kept each sentence to what idea-repo's notes say that paper supports.
- **Checks in Section 5, from experiment-repo's new scripts:**
  - **Centred Brier:** centring changes the ceiling reference by 0.004 in interpolation and 0.024 in extrapolation, so it does not explain the interpolation gap.
  - **Ridge:** on a balanced design its extrapolation bias slope is about half that of the IRT model (−0.27 against −0.61), but on a uniform design it is not (−0.54). The text says we did not test why.
  - I asked experiment-repo (`experiment-repo`#10) to confirm both sentences say what its files compute.
- **Internal names in `code/`:** experiment-repo says its grep is clean at `0a40bc0`, which is now in `dev`. I didn't grep it myself.
- **Still waiting:**
  - figtab-repo hasn't answered `figtab-repo`#7, the renumbering request so the file names match the paper's Tables 8 and 9. I'll change the `\input` paths when it lands.
  - experiment-repo's public-baseline runs (the review's M6) are queued behind a loaded host.
